prompt:
A sheet of seven HUD weapon glyphs for a space-combat game. Flat, very dark navy background (#0a1020). One row of seven equal square cells, each glyph large and centred in its cell, with a small off-white caption under each, in this order: LASERS, TURBO LASERS, CHARGE LASERS, RAILGUN, MISSILES, RIPPERS, CONCUSSION.
Image 1 is the STYLE reference: thin off-white strokes, sharp angular cuts, interrupted and offset strokes, confident asymmetric composition, every stroke terminal sliced flat. Copy its line quality and attitude, not its symbols.
Image 2 is the CONTENT reference: keep each glyph's idea but redraw it with far more character. Lasers: two parallel steep slashes of unequal length. Turbo lasers: three such slashes. Charge lasers: a single slash held between two angular brackets. Railgun: one heavy slash flanked by two thin full-length guide lines. Missiles: a sharp open arrowhead on a dashed diagonal trail. Rippers: three small open chevron rounds streaming up the same diagonal. Concussion: a small diamond with five radiating cut ticks.
Images 3 and 4 show the game's HUD mood: quiet, precise futuristic instruments. Match that restraint.
Rules: all slashes share one steep axis about 63 degrees from horizontal; one stroke weight throughout; flat, no glow, no gradients, no circles, no soft curves; no literal guns or missile silhouettes; the seven must read as one family built from the same construction, yet each distinct in silhouette and guessable at a glance; readable when shrunk to 24 pixels. Vector-crisp edges, no texture.
No boxes or frames around the glyphs: unity comes from the shared axis, stroke and terminals only.
model_text:
I have created a comprehensive sheet of seven distinct HUD weapon glyphs for your space-combat game, meticulously adhering to the strict design constraints you provided. 

Each glyph in the row—from the precise steep slashes of the Lasers and Railgun to the angular complexity of the Concussion diamond—was constructed with thin, vector-crisp lines and flat-sliced terminals to mirror the aggressive, cut-stroke aesthetic you requested. By applying a consistent 63-degree axis and one stroke weight across all symbols, I've ensured they function as a single visual family while maintaining individual character and instant recognizability.

The flat off-white forms against the very dark navy background match the quiet and precise mood of your game’s futuristic instruments, and I've ensured they remain perfectly legible at any scale. I hope this final design serves as the ideal precise instrument for your game's user interface.
